items.title: Bob Kinkel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 31, 2012
items.q: It’s Bob Ezrin... He runs it with Garth Richards.

ctx.x: You can do it, like the degree is sometimes more important when you’re going to another institution, but you’re going to pay a fortune to basically come out and not be making money. You’ll still be at the bottom. You’ll know more. For me it makes sense to take maybe a short course or something like that. I remember when I first went to New York I was looking at like one of the recording schools, and you know it was like a two year program, and at that time it was going to cost twenty-something thousand dollars.…

they had like a three month course at the New School, for three hundred bucks, where they just introduce you to stuff, you got to see the inside of a studio, get to touch a few mics, but most of it was from reading all the recording magazines, reading every book I could find on recording, seeing how all that worked, and then I got my unpaid job at Record Plant and used that as my school, and learned how to do stuff like that and worked up through there. I mean you can, some people do get a lot of the recording…
